status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Identify, select and initiate moderating responses, evaluate the resulting safety state, report deviations and decide whether to request continued execution.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The March 2026 Apollo Go fleet incident concerns correlated temporary stoppage in live traffic; passengers exited safely, while the failure pathway is unresolved. For IEEE-7009 8.3 DIOP4, the missing applicability fact is whether the relevant system implemented IEEE 7009’s fail-safe design-in-operation process and Clause 6 prerequisites for this moderation sequence; stopping, rollback or attempted abort does not establish that design undertaking, and a continuation request is conditional rather than always mandatory. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: The autonomous vehicles stopped in live traffic and passengers exited safely after responders arrived. The source does not identify the moderating-response decisions, resulting safety-state evaluation or continuation decisions. Safe passenger exit alone does not resolve those fail-safe operations.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: More than 100 robotaxis stopped during normal live traffic operation, stranding passengers and requiring police and company response. The fleet did not function appropriately in that operating context. The result covers the reported stoppage and disruption. No injuries or specific failing component are established.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide processes and procedures for safely decommissioning and phasing out AI systems without increasing risks or decreasing organizational trustworthiness.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The March 2026 Apollo Go fleet incident concerns correlated temporary stoppage in live traffic; passengers exited safely, while the failure pathway is unresolved. The evidenced event was temporary fleet stoppage and passenger recovery during a system failure. It was not decommissioning, phasing out or discontinuing the AI system’s use, the lifecycle activity governed by GOVERN 1.7.

review.reason_for_change: The fleet stoppage and rescue response are not permanent decommissioning or phase-out of the AI systems.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence demonstrates a material correlated-failure mode in embodied autonomous infrastructure: a shared system failure can simultaneously immobilise a large fleet in live road environments. Without a confirmed root cause, VIGIL does not infer whether the mechanism involved central control, communications, cloud infrastructure, fleet orchestration or vehicle-local software. Stopped vehicles and safe passenger exit do not establish the execution/continuation decisions needed for bounded safe-exit success. That role becomes ambiguous; control availability/state remain unresolved. The outage’s root cause and repair remain unknown, and no external requirement candidate is independently established.
